title: Customer Feedback Playbook: Mini Synthesis & Rapid Feature Plays (Fall 2028)
content:
Context and goal:
Quick, engineering-friendly synthesis of recent customer signal (Aug–Oct 2028) focused on high-velocity plays we can prototype and ship in a single sprint or two. This is intentionally a compact playbook for product/solutions to triage with engineering partners.

Method / sources used:
- 42 raw customer conversations (CS triage notes) from Aug–Oct 2028
- NPS follow-ups from top 20 customers (re-sent short survey + interview)
- Observability spikes (Console traces) for slow-route incidents: Aug–Sep 2028
- Partner field notes from Solutions Eng (3 calls)

High-level themes (one-liners):
1) Predictable cost controls: customers want a simple way to cap monthly inference spend per-app and per-model without losing traffic.
2) Model-fallback transparency: requests failing over to cheaper/alternate models cause unexplained quality drops and trust issues; they want visibility and opt-out.
3) Token accounting mismatch: discrepancies between Console token counts and invoice for a subset of customers (esp. with streaming + function calls).
4) Faster local repro for Private deployments: platform teams require a reproducible devkit that matches our Dedicated runtime for perf regressions.
5) Short-run prompt evaluation tools: product teams want quick A/B tools to measure quality delta across quantized variants at low cost.

Representative customer quotes (trimmed):
- “We turned on fallback during Black Friday and the app answered weirdly — no way to see what fallback model ran.” — e-comm analytics startup
- “Our devs spend hours reproducing latency spikes; a local runtime parity would save weeks.” — fintech platform
- “Billing doesn't line up for complex agent flows — we can't justify the margin without trust in counts.” — midmarket SaaS

Microplays (rapid feature proposals) — prioritized by expected impact / time-to-value
A. Spend cap per-route (Low dev, High impact)
- What: Add per-route monthly spend caps with soft/ hard modes: soft = send warning + thin degrade; hard = throttle requests once cap exceeded.
- Why: Reduces surprise invoices and enables safe PLG adoption.
- Rough engineering estimate: 1 sprint for API + console flagging + account-level metric; 1.5 sprints if rate-limit infra work needed.
- Owner suggestion: product-hosted-api + billing infra
- Risk/notes: need accurate token accounting first (see theme 3).

B. Fallback audit trail & opt-out toggle (Medium dev, High trust)
- What: Per-request header + Console trace that records fallback decision (which model, reason, cost delta), plus tenant-level toggle to opt out of auto-fallbacks.
- Why: Restore trust, enable root-cause for quality regressions after rollouts.
- Estimate: 2 sprints (serving-runtime + console integration).
- Linked-ticket: JIRA-CC-9123 (initial spec exists)

C. Streaming token reconciliation quickfix (Medium dev, Medium impact)
- What: Reconcile token counts by adding an optional streaming token debug flag (emit per-chunk token delta to logs + invoice reconciliation export).
- Why: Attack immediate billing mismatch reports; helps SREs and Billing to trace flows.
- Estimate: 1 sprint + small billing export change.
- Short-term mitigation: offer manual reconciliation reports for affected customers (CS workflow).

D. Private devkit parity snapshot (Large dev, High enterprise impact)
- What: Distributable dev image and benchmarks that reproduce Dedicated/Private execution path (quantization flags, kernel selection toggles, KV-cache profiles).
- Why: Reduces platform-team onboarding time and incident turnaround for Private customers.
- Estimate: 3–5 sprints (eng+infra+docs).
- Suggested owner: private-deployments + serving-runtime + solutions-eng.

E. Mini-eval runner for quantized model A/B (Low dev, Medium impact)
- What: Console feature: run a small evaluation harness (sample prompts + automatic scoring) comparing two model/quant settings and show cost delta + quality delta.
- Why: Enables product teams to pick quant settings confidently.
- Est: 1 sprint (console + small infra).

Priority matrix snapshot (informal):
- Quick wins: A, C, E
- Trust/regulatory: B
- Strategic enterprise: D

Edgecases & open questions (to resolve before committing)
- Q1: How many customers would actually use per-route spend caps vs account-level caps? (Action: CS to run short poll with top 25 active accounts by spend; owner: Asha)
- Q2: If we surface fallback details, are there privacy/PGP concerns for inference content? (Action: Security review; owner: security-and-compliance)
- Q3: Does streaming token debug flag change performance characteristics? (Action: SRE to bench; owner: site-reliability-engineering)

Operational playbook snippets (tactical)
- For immediate billing disputes: offer a reconciled CSV export (include per-request model id, tokens, timestamps) and a 7-day SLA for manual reconciliation for large customers.
- For fallbacks seen in production: enable fallback audit on tenant and re-run sample session with debug dump.
- For Private customers: schedule a "parity workshop" (2-hour working session) to capture missing ops steps and sample workflows.

Suggested metrics to track post-implementation:
- Reduction in billing dispute tickets (count per month).
- Time-to-resolution for latency incidents (median hours).
- Number of tenants opting out of fallback (proxy for trust).
- % of Private onboarding incidents reduced after devkit release.

Quick cost/benefit callouts (back-of-envelope):
- Spend cap (A): prevents 3–5 large surprise invoices annually -> expected reduction in churn risk for top 30 customers (~$300–$450k ARR risk mitigated).
- Fallback audit (B): builds trust and reduces escalations; intangible but high for enterprise deals.

Draft rollout recommendation (minimal viable path)
1) Triage token accounting fixes and add streaming debug flag (C) — blocker for accurate spend cap and billing reconciliation. 2) Implement per-route spend cap (A) with soft mode first. 3) Implement fallback audit trail + opt-out (B) in parallel with A if resources permit. 4) Plan Private devkit (D) as Q1 2029 initiative with solutions-eng run pilot.

Resources/people to loop in immediately:

- Security: Priyanka Rao

Unresolved / notes-to-self:

- Cross-check JIRA-CC-9123 scope vs the proposed fallback audit to avoid duplication.
- Add short CS survey draft to capture interest in spend caps; aim to send 2028-11-12.

Next steps (this doc is intentionally compact):

- Eng to provide rough feasibility notes within 1 week.
